# Datasets

## Spawn timing data

Spawn timing data for Chinook salmon were collected from 2001 to 2005 in the MFSR. Because redds were not observed daily, we inferred spawn dates as the initial date (day of year) a completed redd was observed. We removed data from 2001, and data from Knapp Creek and Cape Horn Creek, as these sites were not consistently sampled. The final dataset contained `r nrow(spawn_data)` georeferenced redds (i.e., inferred spawn date) across `r length(unique(spawn_data$COMID))` stream reaches (i.e., COMIDs), nested within six major spawning tributaries that also included Beaver Creek (tributary to Marsh Creek) and Elk Creek (tributary to Bear Valley Creek), totaling eight spawning streams across four years. We spatially joined each redd GPS location to the NHDPlus Version 2 to assign stream reaches based on a common identifier (COMID). The COMID is used to link redd data with covariate data associated with the stream reach on which it is located.

**Grouping Structure**

```{r comids}
n_sparse_COMIDS_5 <- spawn_data |>
  count(COMID, name = "n_redds") |>
  filter(n_redds < 5) |>
  nrow()
n_sparse_COMIDS_2 <- spawn_data |>
  count(COMID, name = "n_redds") |>
  filter(n_redds <= 2) |>
  nrow()

n_perc_1 <- spawn_data |>
  count(COMID, name = "n_redds") |>
  filter(n_redds <= 1) |>
  nrow() / length(unique(spawn_data$COMID)) * 100

n_perc_2 <- spawn_data |>
  count(COMID, name = "n_redds") |>
  filter(n_redds <= 2) |>
  nrow() / length(unique(spawn_data$COMID)) * 100

n_perc_5 <- spawn_data |>
  count(COMID, name = "n_redds") |>
  filter(n_redds <= 5) |>
  nrow() / length(unique(spawn_data$COMID)) * 100
```

The structure of the data is repeated measures on COMIDs, and multiple years, shared across COMIDs within streams. Many `COMIDs` only have 1-2 observation (@fig-comid-counts). There are `r n_sparse_COMIDS_5` COMIDs with \<5 redds (`r round(n_perc_5, 1)`%), `r n_sparse_COMIDS_2` with \<= 2. (`r n_perc_2`%).

```{r fig-comid-counts, fig.width=6, fig.height=2, fig.cap="Number of observations (redds) per COMID."}
p.counts1 <- spawn_data |>
  distinct(stream, COMID) |>
  count(stream, name = "n_COMIDs") |>
  arrange(desc(n_COMIDs)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(stream, -n_COMIDs), y = n_COMIDs, fill = stream)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols.streams) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Count of COMIDs") +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

p.counts2 <- spawn_data |>
  count(COMID, name = "n_redds") |>
  arrange(n_redds) |>
  ggplot(aes(n_redds)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 10, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Number of redds", y = "Count of COMIDs")

p.counts1 | p.counts2 +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

\newpage

**Distribution of spawn timing**

Spawn timing is generally unimodal, with a peak in late August to early September (@reffig-spawn-dist A). The distribution is slightly left-skewed, but the mean and median are similar, indicating low skewness, and the variance is low with no evidence of overdispersion. There is also substantial variation in spawn date by stream and year (@fig-spawn-dist B-C; @fig-temp-dist-spawn) and within COMIDs within streams (@fig-spawn-comid).

```{r fig-spawn-dist, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide', fig.width=8, fig.height=6, out.width="80%", fig.cap = "Histogram and density of spawn timing for all streams and years (A), and by stream (B) and year (C). In panel (A), colored, vertical lines indicate the mean spawn date for each year., and the black vertical line indicates the global mean."}

yr_means <- spawn_data |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(yday))

p1 <- ggplot(spawn_data, aes(x = fixed_date + yday)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    bins = 25, fill = "gray80", color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_density(color = "black", size = 1.2, adjust = 1.5) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = fixed_date + mean(yday)),
    color = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    data = yr_means,
    aes(xintercept = fixed_date + mean, color = year), linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.years) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%d %b") +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = fixed_date + 270, y = .06, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 4.5,
    label = paste0(
      "mean = ", round(mean(spawn_data$yday), 2), "\n",
      "median = ", round(median(spawn_data$yday), 2), "\n",
      "min = ", round(min(spawn_data$yday), 2), "\n",
      "max = ", round(max(spawn_data$yday), 2), "\n",
      "var = ", round(var(spawn_data$yday), 2), "\n",
      "SD = ", round(sd(spawn_data$yday), 2)
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    # title = "Histogram and Density of Spawn Dates",
    x = "",
    y = "Density function\n of spawn dates",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(.1, .65),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.box.background = element_rect(colour = "black")
  )

p2 <- spawn_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fixed_date + yday, y = stream, fill = stream)) +
  ggridges::geom_density_ridges() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols.streams) +
  expand_limits(y = c(1, 9)) +
  labs(y = "", x = "") +
  guides(fill = "none")

p3 <- spawn_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fixed_date + yday, y = year, fill = year)) +
  ggridges::geom_density_ridges() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols.years) +
  expand_limits(y = c(1, 6)) +
  labs(y = "", x = "") +
  guides(fill = "none")

p1 / (p2 + p3) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")

path <- here::here("plots", "Figure_02")
ggsave(
  glue::glue("{path}.pdf"),
  plot = last_plot(),
  device = cairo_pdf,
  scale = 1.2,
  width = 18,
  height = 15,
  units = "cm"
)
pdftools::pdf_convert(
  pdf = glue::glue("{path}.pdf"),
  filenames = glue::glue("{path}.png"),
  format = "png",
  dpi = 300
)
```

**Cumulative proportion of redds over time**

The temporal progression of Chinook salmon spawning activity varied within each stream across the four study years (@fig-spawn-cum)). The cumulative proportion of redds provides an intuitive measure of the spawning season's pace and timing. Streams like Marsh and Sulphur exhibit rapid increases, suggesting short, concentrated spawning windows. In contrast, streams like Big and Camas show more gradual increases, indicating a more protracted spawning season. Year-to-year variation is evident in several streams. Overall, this figure highlights both spatial and temporal heterogeneity in spawn timing that underpins the need for models incorporating stream- and year-specific effects.

```{r fig-spawn-cum, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, out.width="80%", results='hide', fig.cap="Proportion of cumulative Chinook salmon redds over time (day of year) across years (2002–2005) and streams. Each line represents a different year, with color denoting the year. Stream-specific panels illustrate temporal variation in the progression of spawning activity, as measured by cumulative redd counts normalized to the maximum value in each stream-year combination."}

props <- spawn_data |>
  select(year, stream, yday) |>
  group_by(year, stream, yday) |>
  add_count() |>
  distinct() |>
  group_by(year, stream) |>
  arrange(year, stream, yday) |>
  mutate(cum_redds = cumsum(n)) |>
  mutate(cum_redds_p = cum_redds / max(cum_redds))

props |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fixed_date + yday, y = cum_redds_p, color = as.factor(year))) +
  ggh4x::facet_wrap2(~stream, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y", axes = "all", strip = strip_vanilla(clip="off")) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.5)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.years, name = "Year") +
  labs(x = "Day of Year", y = "Proportion of ccumulative redds", color = "")

path <- here::here("plots", "Figure_03")
ggsave(
  glue::glue("{path}.pdf"),
  plot = last_plot(),

  height = 8,
  units = "cm"
)
pdftools::pdf_convert(

  filenames = glue::glue("{path}.png"),
  format = "png",
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Covariate Derivation and Screening

The initial focal covariates included stream temperature (°C), stream discharge (cms), elevation (m), and stream slope (unitless). 

**Stream temperature**

We used modeled daily average stream temperature values predicted at the stream segment (COMID) scale (Siegel et al. 2023). These data were downloaded and filtered to 2002-2005 and for the MFSR (@fig-plot-temp-regime).

```{r fig-temp-regime, fig.width=7, fig.height=6, out.width="90%", fig.cap="Modeled thermal regimes (2001-2005) for MFSR tributaries."}
df_temp_stream <- df_temp |>
  group_by(stream, yday) |>
  summarise(
    mean    = mean(temp),
    temp_40 = quantile(temp, probs = 0.4),
    temp_60 = quantile(temp, probs = 0.6),
    temp_min = min(temp),
    temp_max = max(temp),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p.temp.quants <- df_temp_stream |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fixed_date + yday)) +
  ggh4x::facet_wrap2(~stream, ncol = 2, axes = "all", strip = strip_vanilla(clip="off")) +
  geom_ribbon(data = df_temp_stream, aes(ymin = temp_min, ymax = temp_max), fill = "grey") +
  geom_ribbon(data = df_temp_stream, aes(ymin = temp_40, ymax = temp_60), fill = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean), color = "black") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Accent") +
  labs(x = "", y = "Daily water temperature (\u00b0C)", color = "Year") +
  theme(axis.title.y = ggtext::element_markdown())

# Summarize: mean daily temp across COMIDs within stream x year x yday
df_temp_summary <- df_temp |>
  group_by(stream, year, yday) |>
  summarise(mean_temp = mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Plot: faceted by stream, lines colored by year
p.temp.annual <- df_temp_summary |>
  # filter(yday >= 180, yday <= 300) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fixed_date + yday, y = mean_temp, color = year)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ stream, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 months", date_labels = "%b") +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.years) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Mean daily stream temperature (°C)",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "italic")
  )
p.temp.annual

```

These modeled temperatures were validated against empirical logger data collected at a subset of sites in the Middle Fork basin, with strong agreement (Pearson correlation coefficient = 0.97; @fig-isaak-siegel).

```{r}
#| label: fig-isaak-siegel
#| fig-cap: "Comparison of Siegel et al. (2023) modeled temperatures with empirical observations from Isaak et al."
#| echo: false

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("plots", "Figure_isaak-siegel-compare.png"))
```

**Streamflow**

Stream flow data were compiled from a single USGS Gage lower in the watershed (MF Salmon River at MF Lodge NR Yellow Pine ID - 13309220; @fig-flow-raw).

```{r fig-flow-raw, fig.width=7, fig.height=6, out.width="90%", fig.cap = "Inter-annual variability in daily discharge (cfs) at MF Lodge USGS Gage 13309220."}
p.flow.1 <- df_flows |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fixed_date + yday, y = flow_cfs, color = year)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.years, name = "Year") +
  labs(
    title = "Linear scale",
    x = "",
    y = "Mean daily discharge (ft<sup>3</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.title.y = ggtext::element_markdown(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(.8, .65),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.box.background = element_rect(colour = "black")
  )

p.flow.2 <- df_flows |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fixed_date + yday, y = flow_cfs, color = year)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.years, name = "Year") +
  labs(title = "Log scale", x = "", y = "") +
  theme(axis.title.y = ggtext::element_markdown(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +
  guides(color = "none")

tmp <- df_flows |>
  group_by(yday) |>
  summarise(
    mean    = mean(flow_cfs),
    flow_40 = quantile(flow_cfs, probs = 0.4),
    flow_60 = quantile(flow_cfs, probs = 0.6),
    flow_10 = quantile(flow_cfs, probs = 0.1),
    flow_90 = quantile(flow_cfs, probs = 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p.flow.3 <- tmp |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fixed_date + yday)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = tmp, aes(ymin = flow_10, ymax = flow_90), fill = "grey") +
  geom_ribbon(data = tmp, aes(ymin = flow_40, ymax = flow_60), fill = "blue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean), color = "red") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Accent") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    subtitle = "Red line = mean, blue ribbon = 40 - 60th percentiles, Grey ribbon = full range",
    x = "",
    y = "Log Daily discharge (ft<sup>3</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>)"
    ) +
  theme(axis.title.y = ggtext::element_markdown())

(p.flow.1 + p.flow.2) / p.flow.3 +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

**Time-windowed temp and flow metrics**

For each redd, we computed several time-windowed summaries of temperature and flow relative to the inferred spawn date:

-   *Antecedent metrics*: average 30-, 60-, and 90-days preceding the spawn date
-   *Spanning metrics*: averages centered on the spawn date
-   *Post-spawn metrics*: average 30-, 60-, and 90-day following the spawn date

The spanning and post-spawn metrics were omitted from further consideration as preliminary data exploration showed weak if any relationship with spawn timing.

**Elevation and slope**

Elevation and stream slope data were available at the COMID (stream reach)scale from the NHDPlus Version 2 (Horizon Systems, 2018).

# Exploratory Data Analysis

## Bivariate relationships

Bivariate relationships between spawn date (`yday`) and continuous predictors (@fig-covars)), and pairwise correlations between all continuous covariates (@fig-colin), are shown below.

```{r fig-covars, fig.width=6, fig.height=5, fig.cap = "Bivariate relationships between spawn date (`yday`) and continuous covariates. Solid lines are linear fits."}
covariates <- c(
  "temp_30", "temp_60", "temp_90",
  "flow_30", "flow_60", "flow_90",
  "mean_elevation", "slope"
)

covariates |>
  map(~ plot_covariate(model_data, .x)) |>
  patchwork::wrap_plots(ncol = 3)
```

```{r fig-colin, fig.width=9, fig.height=8, out.width="80%", fig.cap="Pairwise correlations between continuous covariates."}
library(ggcorrplot)

model_data |>
  select(temp_30, temp_60, temp_90, flow_30, flow_60, flow_90, mean_elevation, slope) |>
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs") |>
  ggcorrplot(
    method = "square",
    type = "lower",
    lab = TRUE,
    lab_size = 3,
    colors = c("#4575b4", "white", "#d73027"),
    outline.color = "white"
  )
```

**Takeaways from Figures**

Among temperature variables, `temp_90` clearly shows the strongest relationship with spawn date (@fig-covars) and is highly colinear with `temp_30` and `temp_60` (@fig-colin), supporting its use as the sole temperature predictor. There is a negative relationship between `mean_elevation` and `yday`, and it is only weakly correlated with `temp_90` (r = 0.31). Flow variables (`flow_30`, `flow_60`, `flow_90`) all show a decaying-exponential relationship with spawn date, with a strong year effect that suggests much of their explanatory signal is redundant with year as a fixed effect. Stream `slope` shows no meaningful relationship with spawn date.

model_data |>

  summarise(

<!-- Reach elevation was considered under two interpretations. First, elevation can serve as a thermal proxy, as stream temperatures decline predictably with elevation across watersheds (Lisi et al. 2003, Isaak and Rieman 2013); however, this interpretation renders elevation redundant when stream temperatures are already included in the model. Second, elevation may reflect a distance or travel-time signal independent of temperature — fish migrating to high-elevation spawning grounds require more time en route, potentially arriving later and completing redds later in the season. Under this interpretation, a positive association between elevation and spawn date would be expected after accounting for temperature.  In the MFSR network, however, these two interpretations cannot be empirically separated: reach elevation and 90-day antecedent temperature were correlated (Figure A2.2), and both showed nearly identical bivariate relationships with spawn timing (Figure A2.6). Critically, elevation variation in this network is structured primarily between tributaries rather than within them — the between-tributary signal is absorbed by stream identity as a fixed effect, while the residual within-tributary elevation gradient adds little explanatory power beyond what is already captured by stream temperature and COMID-level random effects. Elevation therefore offered no independent explanatory contribution and was excluded from the candidate model set. -->

## `flow_90`

Annual streamflow conditions were considered because high-discharge years may impede upstream migration, delaying adult arrival on spawning grounds and pushing redd completion dates later in the season. We indexed flow using 30-, 60-, and 90-day averages prior to, during, and following the inferred spawn date at each redd location using discharge from a USGS gauge near the mouth of the Middle Fork (gauge 13309220). Because this gauge is downstream of all study reaches, the discharge index lacked spatial resolution across tributaries; moreover, year-to-year variation dominated its signal, producing strong collinearity with the year fixed effect (VIF > 1000 in models including both), which precluded independent inference on flow conditions. Discharge was therefore excluded from further consideration

```{r fig-flow-90, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, out.width="90%", fig.cap = "Spawn timing vs. 90-day mean discharge pre spawn at MF Lodge."}
ggplot(model_data, aes(x = flow_90, y = fixed_date + yday, color = year)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.years) +
  labs(x = "90-day mean\nflow (CFS) pre spawn", y = "Spawn date") +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +

ggplot(model_data, aes(x = flow_90, y = fixed_date + yday, color = stream)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.streams) +
  labs(x = "90-day mean\n flow (CFS) pre spawn", y = "Spawn date") +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +

  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

### Why `flow_90` is problematic

Not spatially resolved

-   We are modeling spawn timing at the redd level (COMID/stream)
-   `flow_90` is calculated from a single downstream gauge
-   This assumes flow conditions are identical across all sites
-   Including it gives the illusion of spatially resolved variation that isn't there

Correlated with year

-   `flow_90` varies mostly across years, strongly confounded with year
-   flow-related signal is probably already captured by year fixed effect
-   Including both `flow_90` and year risks collinearity

Spawn-time aligned flow does not equal experienced flow

-   While `flow_90` is aligned to each redd's spawn date, it reflects a low basin gauge, not actual hydrologic conditions experienced at the redd site
-   So it might be precisely wrong — aligned in time but irrelevant in space

\newpage
